questions.question: Shifting to a lower gear has an effect similar to:
questions.explanation: Downshifting to a lower gear slows down your motorcycle.

questions.question: When carrying a passenger, tell them to:

options.text: Sit as far back as possible.
Put their feet on the muffler.
Mount the motorcycle after you start the engine.

questions.correctAnswerText: Mount the motorcycle after you start the engine.
questions.explanation: Your passenger should get on only after you start the engine. They should sit as far forward as possible without crowding you and hold onto your waist, hips, or belt. Their feet should stay on the footrests at all times, even when stopped.

questions.question: One way to know your rear tire is flat while riding is:

options.text: You hear a hissing noise from the rear.
The back end jerks from side to side.

questions.correctAnswerText: The back end jerks from side to side.
questions.explanation: If your rear tire fails, the back of your motorcycle will jerk side to side. Riders rarely hear a tire fail.

questions.question: You should keep enough distance between you and other vehicles to:

options.text: Have time and space to spot and react to hazards.
Allow traffic counters to count you accurately.
Encourage other drivers to cut you off.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have time and space to spot and react to hazards.
questions.explanation: Good following distance gives you room to stop or swerve if the vehicle ahead stops suddenly. It also helps you see hazards like potholes.

questions.question: If your front tire goes flat while riding:

options.text: There will be no change in steering.
The ride will feel too smooth.

questions.explanation: A flat front tire causes heavy steering. If your steering feels heavy, pull off the road and check your tires.

questions.question: To adjust for a passenger's weight, you should:

options.text: Keep a shorter following distance than when riding alone.
Brake later than you would alone.

questions.explanation: The extra weight means your motorcycle needs more time to speed up, slow down, and turn. Reduce your speed, start braking earlier, increase following distance, and find bigger gaps in traffic.

questions.question: When braking, you should:

options.text: Only use the rear brake on wet pavement.

questions.explanation: Use both brakes every time you slow down or stop, no matter the road condition.

questions.question: Why should a load be placed low on a motorcycle?

options.text: A high load raises the center of gravity.
A high load may block the turn signals.
It is hard to see over a high load.
Others cannot see a low load.

questions.correctAnswerText: A high load raises the center of gravity.
questions.explanation: A high load raises your motorcycle's center of gravity and can upset its balance.

questions.question: Your lane position should do all of the following, except:

options.text: Help you avoid other drivers' blind spots.
Help you avoid being seen by other drivers.
Help you be seen by other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Help you avoid being seen by other drivers.
questions.explanation: Good lane position helps you see others and be seen. It keeps you out of blind spots, avoids hazards, protects your lane, shows your intentions, avoids wind blasts, and gives you escape routes.

questions.question: If a dog is chasing you, you should:

options.text: Approach it slowly, then speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Approach it slowly, then speed up.
questions.explanation: If a dog chases you, downshift and slowly approach it. Once close, accelerate and leave it behind. Do not kick it.

questions.question: What is the only way to reduce the effects of alcohol?
questions.explanation: Your liver removes alcohol at a fixed rate. Nothing can speed this up. Only time will reduce alcohol's effects.

questions.question: When carrying a passenger in a sidecar, you should:

options.text: Start slowing down sooner than usual.
Start slowing down later than usual.
Brake harder than usual to stop quickly.
Brake softer than usual to protect the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Start slowing down sooner than usual.
questions.explanation: A passenger in a sidecar adds weight. This changes how your motorcycle handles and stops. You need more space to stop completely.

questions.question: What formation should a group of riders use when entering a curve?
questions.explanation: Use single-file formation when taking curves, turning, or entering or exiting a highway. Staggered formation works for normal riding but not for curves.

questions.question: Which of these do you NOT need to check before riding?

options.text: Testing both brake controls to make sure the brake light works.

questions.explanation: Before riding, check your tires, oil, and fluids. Make sure your headlight, taillight, signal lights, and brake light all work. Paint scratches do not affect safety.

questions.question: When approaching a blind intersection, you should:

options.text: Position your motorcycle so other drivers can see you as soon as possible.
Stay in the left lane to avoid oncoming traffic.
Weave slightly in your lane to be more visible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Position your motorcycle so other drivers can see you as soon as possible.
questions.explanation: Move to the part of your lane where oncoming drivers will see you earliest. For example, move left in your lane when approaching a blind corner on your right.

questions.question: Which of these can be a rectangular sign?
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs like speed limits are rectangular with white background and black lettering. You must follow the rules on these signs.

questions.question: What does this hand signal mean?
questions.explanation: A left arm extended straight out means the rider plans to turn left or change lanes to the left.

questions.question: Braking in a turn is:

options.text: Easier than braking on a straight road.
More difficult than braking on a straight road.
Safe using only the front brake.
Safe using only the rear brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: More difficult than braking on a straight road.
questions.explanation: Braking in a turn is harder than braking on a straight road. You can use both brakes in a turn, but you need proper technique and careful control.

questions.question: How much stopping power comes from the front brake?
questions.explanation: The front brake is stronger than the rear brake. It provides about three-quarters of the motorcycle's total stopping power.

questions.question: As you slow or stop, you should:
questions.explanation: Shift down through the gears as you slow or stop. When stopped, stay in first gear so you can move quickly if needed.

questions.question: A wobble or shaking of the front wheel and handlebars may be caused by:

options.text: Brakes that are not working properly.

questions.explanation: Most wobbles are caused by improper loading, unsuitable accessories, or incorrect tire pressure.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers to upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield:

options.text: Is not necessary if you have a windshield.
Protects more than just your eyes.
Does not protect your face as well as goggles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Protects more than just your eyes.
questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your entire face, including your eyes. Goggles protect only your eyes. A windshield is not an adequate substitute for either.

questions.question: When riding in fog, you should:

options.text: Alternate between the low and high beams.

questions.explanation: Use your low beam headlight in fog. Do not use high beams when riding near other vehicles.

questions.question: Which of the following is not a type of protective riding gear?

options.text: Boots that go above the ankle
Pants made of a soft material

questions.correctAnswerText: Pants made of a soft material
questions.explanation: Protective gear includes a jacket and pants made of leather or sturdy material, footwear that covers and supports your ankles, and hearing protection even with a helmet.
